fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is direct addition of 1–3 wt.% MoS2 to bare CoCrFeNi, whereas the target varies matrix Mo content in a multicomponent Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 composite.

The assertion that MoS2 remains thermally stable and lubricating in ambient air up to 800 °C is incorrect; high-temperature performance depends on oxidation and formation of oxide/silver-molybdate tribofilms.
No supporting prior evidence is cited despite the explicit request.
The baseline is unmodified CoCrFeNi rather than the relevant Mo0.2 composite, so the predicted comparison does not reconstruct the study.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the wide-temperature tribology problem and correctly identifies low-shear MoS2 tribofilm formation as a plausible low-temperature mechanism. It also proposes a reasonably controlled comparator experiment with friction, wear, SEM/EDS, and Raman/XPS measurements. However, it misses the central intervention—varying dissolved Mo and Mo-rich sigma-phase content within an SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox–Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 composite—and omits solid-solution and second-phase strengthening, Ag lubrication, and high-temperature oxide/molybdate glaze formation. Its 10 N condition differs from the target 8 N test, and counterface, speed, distance, processing, and discrete temperatures are unspecified. The blanket prediction of improvement at every temperature also misses the observed intermediate-temperature friction/wear maxima and composition-dependent tradeoff between Mo0.5 friction and Mo1 wear. Most importantly, the high-temperature stability rationale for MoS2 in air is scientifically unsound and unsupported by citations.
